LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 ADJECTIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Which words do we use to describe people, things, and places?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly
2. use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives

Teach
• Focus skill: identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words do we use to describe people, things, and places?
2. How do we compare people, things, and events?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
